explainer_reply:
Looking at these examples, the activated tokens span wildly different domains (economics, code, math, citations, fiction, science), but the tokens themselves share a clear identity: they are almost exclusively high-frequency function words ("the", "of", "and", "a", "to", "is", "in", "that") and punctuation marks (".", ",", "?", ":", parentheses, newlines). The strongest activations tend to be on "the" and sentence-ending periods. Content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives specific to the topic) are consistently not activated.

[EXPLANATION]: Common English function words (articles, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliary verbs—especially "the") and punctuation marks (periods, commas, newlines) across diverse text domains; the neuron fires on high-frequency grammatical tokens rather than content words.
